extracted.intended_audience: astronomers and natural philosophers (practical celestial mechanicians)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and methodological standards for determining and correcting cometary trajectories from observations, plus overarching experimental-philosophy criteria (deduction from phenomena, rejection of unsupported hypotheses) for celestial mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventam cometce trajectoriam corrigere (overall procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: PROPOSITIO XLII. PROBLEMA XXII. Inventam cometce trajectoriam corrigere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-step correction procedure: (1) Assume the plane of the previously found trajectory; select three comet places from the most accurate observations and as widely separated as possible; denote times between observations A and B. Find true comet places in the assumed plane by trigonometric operations. From those true places, about the sun, describe the conic section (per arithmetical operations of prop. xxi lib. i) and let D and E be the areas cut off by radii to the found places (D area between 1st & 2nd obs., E between 2nd & 3rd). Let T be the total time in which the entire area D+E should be described by the comet's velocity (per prop. xvi lib. i). (2) Increase the longitude of the nodes of the trajectory-plane by an amount P (20' or 30'), preserve inclination; compute three true places in this new plane and the areas d & e and total time t. (3) Keep node longitude as in (1) and increase inclination by Q (20' or 30'); compute three true places and areas S & e and total time t. Then form proportions and solve for integers m and n (via the given relations) to obtain corrected inclination and node longitude; from corrected transverse side compute the comet's periodic time. (Includes iterative adjustments and algebraic relations given in the original text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of observational points
rubrics_metrics.description: seligantur tria loca cometae observationibus accuratissimis definita & ab invicem quam maxime distantia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose three observed positions that are (a) defined by the most accurate observations available and (b) as widely separated from one another as possible. Prefer observations where the comet is in or near perigee (or at least not far from perigee). From these apparent places, compute true places in the assumed trajectory plane using trigonometric operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a conic through three true places and use areas to relate to times
rubrics_metrics.description: per loca illa inventa, circa centrum solis ceu umbilicum, per operationes arithmeticas ope prop. xxi lib. i institutas, describatur sectio conica : & ejus areae, radiis a sole ad loca inventa ductis terminatse, sunto D & E ; nempe D area inter observationem primam & secundam, & E area inter secundam ac tertiam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given three true heliocentric places, construct the conic section (parabola/ellipse/hyperbola as appropriate) passing through them (using the arithmetic methods referenced). Compute the areas subtended by radii to each successive pair of places (D and E). Use Kepler's area-time relation (prop. xvi lib. i) to equate area proportions with elapsed times (total time T for D+E). This provides quantitative constraints to correct the assumed orbit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment by varying node longitude and inclination (iterative corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Augeatur longitudo nodorum plani trajectoriae, additis ad longitudinem illam 20' vel 30' quae dicantur P ; & servetur plani illius inclinatio ad planum eclipticae. ... Servetur longitudo nodorum in operatione prima, & augeatur inclinatio plani trajectoriae ad planum eclipticae, additis ad inclinationem illam 20' vel 30', quae dicantur Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively alter the guessed orbital parameters: in one trial increase node longitude by P (20' or 30') while holding inclination fixed; in another trial increase inclination by Q while holding node longitude fixed. For each trial compute true places and corresponding areas and times. These perturbed computations supply the data needed to set up linear relations and solve for integer multipliers to correct the initial guess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve for integer multipliers to obtain true inclination and node
rubrics_metrics.description: signis + & — probe observatis quaerantur numeri m & n ea lege, ut sit ... Et si in operatione prima I designet inclinationem plani trajectoriae ad planum eclipticse & K longitudinem nodi alterutrius, erit I + nQ vera inclinatio plani trajectoriae ad planum eclipticse & K + mP vera longitudo nodi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form the algebraic relations (as given) linking the computed quantities from the three operations and solve for integers m and n such that the relations hold. Use these integers to correct the initial guessed inclination I and node longitude K: true inclination = I + n·Q and true node longitude = K + m·P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute rectum and transverse axes and deduce the periodic time
rubrics_metrics.description: si in operatione prima, secunda ac tertia, quantitates R, r & jo designent latera recta trajectoriae, & quantitates eiusdem latera transversa respective : erit R-^-mr—^n R verum latus rectum, & ... verum latus transversum trajectoriæ quam cometa describit. Dato autem latere transverso datur etiam tempus periodicum cometae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the sets of 'recta' and 'transversa' measurements computed in the three operations, apply the provided linear combinations/formulae (involving the solved m and n) to obtain the true 'latus rectum' and 'latus transversum' of the orbit. The transverse semi-axis (latus transversum) yields the comet's periodic time (period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple apparitions to determine periodic times and transverse axes accurately
rubrics_metrics.description: cometarum revolventium tempora periodica & orbium latera transversa haud satis accurate determinabuntur, nisi per collationem cometarum inter se, qui diversis temporibus apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine a comet's period and the transverse axes of its orbit reliably, compare trajectories computed from observations of the comet appearing at different epochs. If several comets, after equal time intervals, are found to have described the same orbit, conclude they are the same comet; use the intervals between apparitions (revolutions) to deduce the transverse axes and then the elliptical orbits. Collation (comparison) across apparitions is essential for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt parabolic hypothesis for many comet trajectories (initial model)
rubrics_metrics.description: computandae sunt igitur cometarum plurium trajectoriæ, ex hypothesi quod sint parabolae. Nam hujusmodi trajectoriæ cum phænomenis semper congruent quamproxime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For computing trajectories of many comets, assume parabolic paths as a working hypothesis when they fit observed phenomena closely (examples cited: comet of 1680, comets of 1664–1665). Use the parabolic assumption for initial computations unless observations force a different conic classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct early-angle anomalies when comet is very fast near perihelion
rubrics_metrics.description: Subducenda tamen sunt minuta duo prima circiter, ubi cometa velocissimus fuit ; id quod fiet auferendo duodecim minuta secunda ab angulo inter nodum ascendentem & periheHum, seu constituendo angulum illum 49''- 27' 18''.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the comet was extremely rapid (near perihelion), subtract approximately the first two small minutes of anomaly in the angle measurements: specifically, remove about 12 seconds ('duodecim minuta secunda') from the angle between the ascending node and perihelion (or adopt the adjusted angle indicated) to improve congruence between theory and observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comet parallax to demonstrate Earth's annual motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Cometae utriusque parallaxis annua insignis fuit, & inde demonstratur motus annuus terrae in orbe magno.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large observed annual parallaxes of comets serve as empirical evidence for the Earth's annual motion about the Sun. Measure comet parallax across observations to infer and confirm terrestrial orbital motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological standard: deduce propositions from phenomena; avoid unsupported hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 hypotheses non fingo. Quicquid enim ex phænomenis non deducitur, hypothesis vocanda est; & hypotheses ... in philosophia experimentali locum non habent. In hac philosophia propositiones deducuntur ex phænomenis, & redduntur generales per inductionem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental philosophy must derive propositions from observed phenomena and generalize by induction. Do not invent metaphysical/physical/mechanical hypotheses that cannot be deduced from phenomena. Treat as unacceptable any explanatory hypothesis not grounded in empirical deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and reject the vortex hypothesis where it contradicts observed phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothesis vorticum multis premitur difficultatibus. Ut planeta unusquisque radio ad solem ducto areas describat tempori proportionales, tempora periodica partium vorticis deberent esse in duplicata ratione distantiarum a sole. ... Motus cometarum sunt summe regulares, & easdem leges cum planetarum motibus observant, & per vortices explicari nequeunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test vortex-based models against concrete phenomena: predicted relations for period-vs-distance, equality of vortex-part periods, preservation of minor vortices about giant planets, and planet axes/rotation must match observations. Because comet motions are very eccentric and move into all regions of the heavens, and because planetary/rotational data disagree with vortex predictions, the vortex hypothesis is inadequate. Use empirical contradictions (listed in text) as grounds to reject such models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gravitation: properties and inverse-square form as modeling standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Oritur utique haec vis a causa aliqua ... quae agit non pro quantitate superficierum particularum, in quas agit (ut solent causæ mechanicæ) sed pro quantitate materiæ solidæ; & cujus actio in immensas distantias undique extenditur, decrescendo semper in duplicata ratione distantiarum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model the force of gravity as arising from the mass of bodies (not surface area), composed additively from constituent particles, extending to large distances, and decreasing in the duplicate (square) ratio of distance. This inverse-square, mass-proportional law is to be used to account quantitatively for celestial and marine motions up to the orbits examined (e.g., out to Saturn and comet aphelia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume vacuum in celestial space; neglect atmospheric resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Projectilia in aere nostro solam aeris resistentiam sentiunt. Sublato aere, ut fit in vacuo Boyliano, resistentia cessat, siquidem pluma tenuis & aurum solidum aequali cum velocitate in hoc vacuo cadunt. Et par est ratio spatiorum coelestium, quae sunt supra atmospheram terrae. Corpora omnia in istis spatiis liberrime moveri debent;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on vacuum experiments (Boyle), treat space above the atmosphere as effectively a vacuum where air resistance is absent; therefore, in celestial mechanics neglect atmospheric resistance and assume bodies move freely under gravitational laws alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect mutual gravitational perturbations and allow for secular changes in comet orbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Cometae, ob magnum eorum numerum & magnam apheliorum a sole distantiam & longam moram in aphellis, per gravitates in se mutuo nonnihil turbari debent, & eorum eccentricitates & revolutionum tempora nunc augeri aliquantulum, nunc diminu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When predicting long-term comet behaviour, account for mutual gravitational interactions among bodies: these will cause small but non-negligible changes in eccentricities and periods over time. Thus do not expect identically repeatable returns; accept modest deviations consistent with mutual perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrestrial/material consequences of cometary and stellar vapours (qualitative causal claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vapores autem, qui ex sole & stellis fixis & caudis cometarum oriuntur, incidere possunt per gravitatem suam in atmosphaeras planetarum & ibi condensari & converti in aquam & spiritus humidos, & subinde per lentum calorem in sales & sulphura & tincturas & limum & lutum & argillam & arenam & lapides & coralla & substantias alias terrestres paulatim migrare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitatively, consider that vapours from the Sun, fixed stars, and comet tails may fall into planetary atmospheres, condense and transform into liquids and salts, and thus over time contribute to terrestrial materials. This is presented as a possible causal mechanism linking celestial and terrestrial phenomena (treated as a hypothesis tied to observed vapor phenomena).
